text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Parliamentary committee suspends ratification of a 1989 economic accord with Jordan. Ties between Kuwait and Jordan were strained over what Kuwait saw as sympathy by Amman with Iraq during its 1990-91 occupation of the Gulf Arab state.
- Police seize 13,388 bottles of alcoholic beverages hidden in shampoo boxes. Alcohol is banned in the conservative state in line with the teachings of Islam.
- Kuwait National Petroleum Company (KNPC) plans environmental improvements at its al-Ahmadi refinary, company official says. Al-Ahmadi is the largest of Kuwait's three domestic refineries.
- Trade and Industry Minister Jassem al-Mudaf discusses trade development with Thailand's ambassaor.

- A group of 19 lawyers form a team to represent opposition parliamentarian Abdullah al-Naibari in a case of a failed attempt against his life. Naibari was injured in his shoulder and jaw when gunmen opened fire at his car on Friday. Kuwait said it had arrested five people in connection with the case.
- Kuwait Stock Exchange's index fell 15.7 points to 2,384.7 on Wednesday.

- MP says the government would propose a bill that would impose charges on some state services. Kuwait's parliament opposes such a measure, seen by some economist as an important element in the state's efforts to eliminate its budegt deficit by the year 2000.
- Kuwait's police arrest an Iraqi national who attempted to enter Kuwait with a forged Qatari passport.
